Subject: Acme - Post-demo model shortlist and next steps

Hi Alice / Bob —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our demo: 

Summary:
- Product: GenAI assistant for internal knowledge retrieval + policy summarization.
- Key constraints: 200–500 token prompts, P95 latency target ~300ms (interactive UI), strict data residency and audit requirements.
- Success criteria: comparable quality to current vendor on summarization rubric, <50% token cost reduction target vs current host, and stable latency under typical concurrency.

Recommended immediate next steps:
1) Redwood runs a short eval using your prompt set (attached link) across 3 candidate models. We’ll provide detailed latency/cost/quality metrics.
2) Align on procurement/terms basics (procurement contact on copy).
3) Technical follow-up: Rishi / Vivek to confirm infra config (KV cache, batching, dedicated vs hosted).

Attached: redwood-model-shortlist.xlsx (shortlist + cost/latency estimates), latency-cost-benchmarks.pdf, demo-recording.mp4. Also linking the prompt set you shared earlier: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1PromptSetExample

Initial model shortlist (high level):
- Llama-2-13b-q8: cost-efficient, low token cost, good baseline quality for summarization. Expected P95 latency: ~240–320ms on dedicated 1-GPU config. Good for scale/cost tradeoffs.
- Falcon-40b-instruct: higher-quality on complex synthesis tasks; higher token and inference cost, P95 latency ~420–600ms. Best if accuracy is the priority.
- Redwood-13b-opt (our tuned 13B): balanced quality and latency; mid-range cost, P95 latency ~280–360ms, often matches Falcon for summarization at lower cost in our benchmarks.

Questions for you: which metric should we prioritize (quality vs cost vs latency)? If you can confirm target P95 and any hard cost ceiling, we’ll tailor the eval.

I’ll schedule a 30-min sync next week to review results — please share 2x slots that work for you.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole

Hi Alice / Bob —

Great questions — answers inline and next steps below.

1) Latency: the Llama-2-13b-q8 numbers are from our dedicated 1xA10-like GPU profile with our continuous-batching disabled for single-interactive requests. That yields ~240–320ms P95 for the 200–500 token prompts you described. If you require a hard <300ms P95 for the most common prompt, we recommend: 
   - Primary eval: Redwood-13b-opt on dedicated nodes (P95 ~280ms expected)
   - Fallback: Llama-2-13b-q8 tuned with our low-latency kernel and aggressive KV caching (P95 can be driven <300ms in many runs)
   - Higher-quality option: Falcon-40b-instruct if you prioritize top-end quality (will need to relax latency expectation or move to larger dedicated config).

2) Data & compliance: yes — we can run the eval in EU region and keep output artifacts in your org's Drive. We’ll limit access to the Redwood eval team and produce the SOC 2 evidence bundle (scope/signed attestation). I’ll have Rishi attach the specific SOC2 checklist and audit artifact list in the follow-up.

3) Prompt set & scoring: yes. We’ll run automated metrics (ROUGE, BERTScore) and coordinate a small manual pass (5 human evals) — we can either use your reviewers or Redwood’s vetted annotators (you pick). Please confirm which you prefer.

Timeline and deliverables:
- Redwood runs eval across 3 candidates (Redwood-13b-opt, Llama-2-13b-q8, Falcon-40b-instruct) using your prompt set by EOD 2026-08-22.
- Deliverables: evaluation workbook (latency/cost/quality), demo recording with sample outputs, and a short recommendation memo.

I’ve attached the evaluation plan to this thread and included links: latency-cost-benchmarks.pdf, redwood-model-shortlist.xlsx, demo-recording.mp4, prompt set: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1PromptSetExample.

Available slot: Tue 8/24 10–11am PT works — I scheduled a 30-min review (invite to follow).

Thanks — cc’ing Rishi and Vivek for the tech run.

Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Forwarding the thread — short internal runbook for the eval run: 

- Goal: run 3 models on Acme prompt set and produce a single workbook with columns: prompt_id, model, token_count, inference_ms (P50/P95), cost_estimate_per_call, rouge, bertscore, manual_quality_score.
- Infra: run in eu-west region per request. Use dedicated small pool (1xA10-type) for consistency. Enable KV cache and set batch size to 1 for interactive latency measurement; run a separate batched run for throughput cost estimates.
- Timeline: start run 8/22 morning (today), finish by EOD 8/22, upload artifacts to https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1BenchmarksExample and share with Acme.
- Notes: Falcon-40b requires larger mem profile; if memory pressure occurs fallback to 2x smaller batch or use a gptq quantized artifact.

Action items:
- Vivek: kick off infra + ensure quantized artifacts ready for Llama/Falcon.
- Marissa: confirm whether Acme wants Redwood annotators for the manual pass or they’ll provide reviewers.
- Rishi: I’ll own the workbook aggregation and the SOC2 artifact list (will attach in next message).

Links: HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/1245789
Attachments for Acme: redwood-model-shortlist.xlsx, latency-cost-benchmarks.pdf
